title: 辩论：民主一定是最好的制度吗？
title_en: Is democracy necessarily the best system?

questions.question: 按这场「民主是不是最好的制度」辩论最后的共识，衡量一套制度最该看什么？
options: 它是否让每一项公共决策都经过全体公民投票表决
它能否稳定地选出最有知识、最有德行的那批人来掌握国家权力
多数人的意见是否在每一次选举中都得到了尊重
它出错之后，能否让错误暴露，并且不流血地把它改过来
questions.explanation: 共识落在：衡量制度不看它选出谁，而看错了以后能不能不流血地改；民主的核心价值在于和平纠错，不在于多数天然正确。总结还明说，好的民主不是让每件事全民表决，而是让目标可争、执行可查、失败可改。
questions.question_en: According to the consensus this debate on whether democracy is the best system reached, what matters most in judging a political system?
options_en: Whether every public decision goes to a vote of all citizens
Whether it reliably puts the most knowledgeable and virtuous people in power
Whether the majority's view is respected in every single election
Whether, after it errs, the error can surface and be corrected without bloodshed
questions.explanation_en: The consensus: judge a system not by whom it picks but by whether its mistakes can be fixed without bloodshed; democracy's core value is peaceful correction, not the majority being right. The summary also says good democracy isn't voting on everything but keeping goals contestable, execution checkable, and failures reversible.

questions.question: 某国选举赢家通吃、社会托底又薄，败选一方屡屡拒不交权。按这场辩论总结的分析，最该从哪里着手？
options: 提高投票率，让选举结果更能代表真正的多数
把争议议题交给专家委员会，减少选举结果的分量
降低失败的不可逆代价，让败选的人还能体面地回到生活
加强全民的公民教育，系统提升选民的素质与理性判断能力
questions.explanation: 总结指出「输了就走」的认账是投票的前提，而肯不肯认输取决于输一次要付多少不可逆的代价：败选若意味着失去医保、房子乃至人身安全，拒不交权就是理性行为，与选民素质无关。所以稳定要到失败的可恢复性里找，而不只是教育和文化。
questions.question_en: In a country where elections are winner-take-all and the safety net is thin, losers keep refusing to hand over power. By this debate's summary, where should a fix start?
options_en: Raise turnout so results better reflect the true majority
Hand contested issues to expert committees to reduce what elections decide
Lower the irreversible cost of losing so the defeated can return to ordinary life with dignity
Strengthen civic education to raise voters' quality and rational judgment
questions.explanation_en: The summary notes that 'lose and leave' is a precondition of voting, and willingness to concede depends on how irreversible a loss is. If defeat means losing health cover, a home, or personal safety, refusing to yield is rational and has nothing to do with voter quality. So stability lies in making failure recoverable, not only in education and culture.

questions.question: 这场辩论的总结如何安排专家、官僚和民意三者的关系？
options: 公众定方向，专业给方案，执行留记录，结果受审查，连成一条闭环
三者天然冲突，只能靠定期选举让它们轮流占据上风
民意至上，专家和官僚只负责不打折扣地执行投票的结果
治国是一门需要知识的技艺，关键决策应交给专家，民意只作为参考意见
questions.explanation: 总结认为专家、官僚、民意不是三组选边站的人：没有行政能力，民主承诺会变空话；没有民主约束，行政能力会变成不受追问的机器。因此要连成闭环。「关键决策交给专家」是辩论中被追问「专家凭什么免于公开辩护」的立场。
questions.question_en: How does the debate's summary arrange the roles of experts, officials, and public opinion?
options_en: The public sets direction, experts propose, execution is recorded, results are reviewed: one closed loop
The three are naturally at odds and can only take turns winning through regular elections
Public opinion is supreme; experts and officials just carry out votes to the letter
Governing is a craft, so key decisions go to experts and public opinion is only advisory
questions.explanation_en: The summary says experts, officials, and the public are not rival camps: without administrative capacity, democratic promises are empty; without democratic checks, capacity becomes an unaccountable machine. Hence a closed loop. 'Leave key decisions to experts' is the position the debate challenged by asking why expertise should be exempt from public justification.
